meta.description: Comprehensive molecular biology toolkit. Use for sequence manipulation, file parsing (FASTA/GenBank/PDB), phylogenetics, and programmatic NCBI/PubMed access (Bio.Entrez). Best for batch processing, custom bioinformatics pipelines, BLAST automation. For quick lookups use gget; for multi-service integration use bioservices.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabrication; accurately describes Biopython library capabilities with correct version information (1.87) and CVE reference

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for computational biology and bioinformatics analysis; clearly directs to gget for quick lookups and bioservices for multi-service integration

methodological_ground.detail: Based on established bioinformatics methods (BLAST, phylogenetics, sequence alignment, structure analysis) with proper tool references

code_usability.detail: All code examples are syntactically correct with proper imports and NCBI Entrez email requirement clearly documented

functional_suitability.note: Exceptional coverage of Biopython capabilities: sequence handling, alignment, databases, BLAST, structure, phylogenetics, motifs with comprehensive reference organization

reliability.note: Excellent reliability documentation including CVE-2025-68463 security advisory, NCBI rate limiting guidance, version pinning recommendations, error handling patterns

performance_context.note: Well-organized documentation with clear modular structure, progressive disclosure through reference files, efficient navigation by capability area

agent_usability.note: Excellent 'When to Use This Skill' section with 11 specific scenarios; clear scope boundaries directing to gget and bioservices for alternatives; comprehensive quick examples for each module

human_usability.note: Clear installation instructions with version pinning, NCBI setup requirements prominently documented, quick examples for each capability area, external tool dependencies noted

security.note: Excellent security practices: CVE advisory with version recommendation, proper NCBI credential management with environment variables, explicit email requirement for NCBI policy compliance

maintainability.note: Excellent structure with version 1.2, license (Biopython License Agreement), current upstream version (1.87), comprehensive reference files, Python version support documented

agent_specific.note: Strong composability with allowed-tools and openclaw metadata; clear module organization; good escape hatches to gget/bioservices; minor: idempotency not explicitly discussed for file operations

key_strengths: Exceptional security awareness with CVE-2025-68463 advisory and explicit version recommendation (1.87+) for untrusted file parsing
Outstanding scope boundary documentation directing users to gget for quick lookups and bioservices for multi-service integration
Comprehensive modular organization covering 7 major capability areas with dedicated reference files for each domain
Excellent NCBI Entrez compliance guidance with required email setting, API key rate limiting, and tool registration best practices
Strong version tracking with current upstream version (1.87), Python compatibility (3.10-3.14, PyPy3.10), and reproducibility via version pinning

recommendations.title: Add E-value filtering example in BLAST section
recommendations.problem: E-value displayed in results but threshold-based filtering not demonstrated
recommendations.root_cause: Quick example focuses on top-N hits rather than quality thresholds
recommendations.fix: Add filtering example: 'significant_hits = [aln for aln in blast_record.alignments if aln.hsps[0].expect < 1e-5]' with explanation of E-value thresholds

recommendations.title: Clarify alignment scoring parameters
recommendations.problem: Gap penalties and match/mismatch scores not shown in alignment quick example
recommendations.root_cause: Example uses default scoring without showing customization
recommendations.fix: Add note to quick example: 'Customize scoring with aligner.match_score, aligner.mismatch_score, aligner.open_gap_score, aligner.extend_gap_score'

recommendations.title: Document PDB atom distance calculation operator
recommendations.problem: Atom subtraction operator (atom1 - atom2) for distance may not be obvious
recommendations.root_cause: Operator overload is convenient but non-standard Python
recommendations.fix: Add explanatory comment in example: '# Atom objects support - operator for Euclidean distance calculation' or show alternative: 'distance = (atom1.coord - atom2.coord).norm()'
